title: Introduce snapshot sharding and preflight migration heuristics
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds snapshot sharding to reduce restore contention for large tenants; introduces a preflight migration heuristic that simulates a dry-run plan and surface incompatible schema shims before upgrade; includes Helm hooks and Terraform state-lock updates to coordinate safe upgrades.
description:
Context and motivation: Large private deployments with many tenant shards were experiencing long restore windows and occasional collisions during parallel restore operations. This PR introduces two orthogonal improvements: (1) snapshot sharding and a shard manager to parallelize backup/restore while preserving restore-order guarantees, and (2) a preflight migration heuristic that computes a conservative migration plan and checks forward/backward schema compatibility to provide deterministic downgrade guards.

What changed (high level): Added a shard_manager to the migrator that assigns stable shard keys and writes a lightweight sequence-lock entry to object storage; extended the migrator plan logic to include a simulated dry-run path that runs compatibility checks (compat_check.go) against pinned schema manifests; added Helm lifecycle jobs to take coordinated local snapshots and to apply preflight checks prior to draining nodes; updated Terraform state-lock module to rotate and verify bucket locks during rolling upgrades. Also added scripts and docs for operators to run a preflight run locally and integrated e2e canary CI to validate an upgrade path.

Checklist (implemented): - [x] Shard manager implementation and unit tests - [x] Preflight dry-run + compatibility assertions - [x] Helm preflight Job + restore hook templates - [x] Terraform state-lock rotation and docs - [x] Operator-facing playbook and examples - [x] E2E canary workflow in CI - [x] Integration tests for migrator plan

Commits (summary): - feat(migrator): add shard manager and sequence-locking for parallel restores - feat(migrator): implement preflight plan simulation and compatibility checks - feat(helm): add preflight job and restore hook templates - chore(terraform): add state-lock rotation module and README - test(migrator): integration tests for plan simulation and shard allocations - docs(upgrades): operator playbook for preflight and emergency rollback

Files changed (high level): - installer/pkg/migrator/*: core logic for planning, shard assignment, sequence-lock write/read, and compatibility assertions. - installer/helm/*: new preflight Job and restore hooks; values file for migration settings. - terraform/modules/state-lock/*: lock rotation, verification, and retention policy. - installer/scripts/take-local-snapshot.sh: utility for air-gapped/local operator snapshot collection. - installer/docs/upgrades.md and examples/private/upgrade-playbook.md: new operator guidance.

Testing and CI: Initial CI run flagged a flaky integration test for cross-shard ordering; addressed by adding deterministic shard key derivation and a small backoff in the restore worker. Final CI run: unit, integration, and e2e canary passed. Canary runs simulated a 3-version upgrade path across a 12-shard tenant and validated sequence-lock enforcement prevented out-of-order restores.

Review conversation (excerpt): - Aisha Kapoor (reviewer): "Can we guarantee sequence-lock entry durability in S3 eventual-consistency windows?" - Author reply: "Added a confirmation loop that verifies object existence and writes a compact manifest entry; for S3 we use checksum+etag verification and retry with exponential backoff." - Liam O'Connor: "Please add a regression test for single-node rollback where shard count changes." - Author: "Added integration test in tests/migrator/integration/plan_test.go to validate shrink/expand shard transitions." - Jonas Müller: "Docs look good; call out operator playbook for emergency `force-restore` steps." - Author: "Expanded upgrade-playbook with explicit force-restore and safe-quarantine steps."

Backward/downgrade guard behavior: The preflight check will fail an upgrade if any pinned schema manifest indicates non-backward-compatible changes and no shim is available. Operators can opt into a "compat-shim" mode (documented) that deploys small translation shims during the migration window; these shims are explicitly time-limited and audited.

Operator impact and notes: - Default behavior is opt-out for shard parallelism; operators must set values.migration.enable_sharding=true to enable. - RPO/RTO considerations included in docs; shard size defaults chosen to balance object store throughput and kube restore concurrency. - The terraform state-lock module must be applied before running the preflight job to ensure lock rotation is active.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag; 2) run canary on internal staging with a 12-shard tenant; 3) surface metrics (restore-latency, sequence-lock-writes, compat-failures) in Console dashboard; 4) enable for customers via release notes and migration-runbook.

Follow-ups: - Add telemetry for shim activation counts and compat failures (ENG-2522). - Explore leader-election alternative for sequence-lock coordination to reduce object store confirmations (ENG-2530).

Merge outcome: PR was merged by squash on 2026-02-18 after two approvals and green CI.
